name: Priorat
summary: Steep Catalan hills where Garnacha and Cariñena grow on llicorella, a dark slate soil. The region is known above all for full-bodied red wines.
label_note: Wines from one village may say 'vino de vila de' and the village name. Single sites may be labelled Paraje, Viña Clasificada or Gran Viña Clasificada, and estate wines 'vino de finca'.

name: Rías Baixas
summary: Galicia's Atlantic coast, where Albariño makes almost all the wine. The whites are light, fresh and high in acidity, often with a saline edge, from vines on granite.
label_note: 'Rías Baixas Albariño' is 100% Albariño. Oak aged whites are sold as 'Rías Baixas barrica'. Subzone names may be used for wines of the subzone.

appellations.name: Val do Salnés
appellations.note: Subzone; label 'Rías Baixas Salnés', at least 70% Albariño, Loureira, Treixadura or Caíño blanco.

appellations.name: Condado do Tea
appellations.note: Subzone; label 'Rías Baixas Condado do Tea', at least 70% Albariño and Treixadura.

appellations.note: Subzone; label 'Rías Baixas Rosal', at least 70% Albariño, Loureira or Caíño blanco.

appellations.note: Subzone; label 'Rías Baixas Ribeira do Ulla'.

name: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry
summary: Fortified wines from the Cádiz coast, made mainly from Palomino grown on white albariza soil and aged in soleras, either under a veil of flor yeast or exposed to air.
pairing: Fino and Manzanilla with fish and seafood.
label_note: Dry styles are Fino, Amontillado, Palo Cortado and Oloroso; sweet ones Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel; blends Pale Dry, Pale Cream, Medium and Cream. Age statements: 12 and 15 years, VOS (20) and VORS (30).

grapes.name: Palomino
grapes.local_note: Palomino Fino or Listán Blanco; the base of the dry styles

grapes.name: Pedro Ximénez
grapes.local_note: Sun dried for the sweet wine of the same name

appellations.name: Fino
appellations.note: Dry; aged only under flor (crianza biológica).

appellations.name: Amontillado
appellations.note: Dry; aged under flor, then with exposure to air.

appellations.name: Palo Cortado
appellations.note: Dry; mainly oxidative ageing after the flor disappears.

appellations.name: Oloroso
appellations.note: Dry; oxidative ageing only.

appellations.name: Pedro Ximénez
appellations.note: Naturally sweet, at least 85% sun dried Pedro Ximénez, aged oxidatively.

appellations.name: Moscatel
appellations.note: Naturally sweet, at least 85% Moscatel.

appellations.name: Pale Dry
appellations.note: Blend based on flor aged wine, under 50 g/l sugar.

appellations.name: Pale Cream
appellations.note: Sweetened blend based on flor aged wine.

appellations.name: Medium
appellations.note: Medium sweet blend.

appellations.name: Cream
appellations.note: Sweet blend, 115 to 140 g/l sugar.

appellations.name: Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda
appellations.note: Separate DO with the same vineyard zone; wines aged only in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, where the flor stays all year.

name: Penedès
summary: Catalan region south west of Barcelona, best known for white and sparkling wines from Xarel·lo, Macabeo and Parellada. Most of Spain's Cava is made here.
pairing: Whites and sparkling wines with fish and seafood.
label_note: Clàssic Penedès is the DO's own traditional method sparkling wine, from organic grapes with at least 15 months on the lees in bottle. 'Vino de Mas' and 'Gran Vino de Mas' mark single estate wines.

appellations.name: Cava
appellations.note: Separate DO spread across several Spanish regions; most of it is made in Penedès, but it is not part of DO Penedès.

appellations.name: Clàssic Penedès
appellations.note: Penedès's own traditional method sparkling wine, organic, at least 15 months from tirage to disgorgement.

name: Rueda
summary: High, flat plateau in Castilla y León where Verdejo makes most of the wine: crisp, herbal whites from deep, well drained soils and a harsh climate.
label_note: 'Gran Vino de Rueda' and 'Fermentado en barrica' are regulated label terms. Dorado and Pálido are the traditional fortified wines.

appellations.name: Dorado
appellations.note: Traditional fortified wine (vino generoso) of Rueda.

appellations.name: Pálido
appellations.note: Traditional fortified wine aged under flor (crianza biológica).

name: Bierzo
summary: In the west of León, Bierzo is known for fragrant, medium-bodied reds from Mencía, often from old vines on slate soils. Godello is the leading white grape.
label_note: Vino de Villa, Vino de Paraje, Viña Clasificada and Gran Viña Clasificada mark wines from one village, one site or one classified vineyard, at lower yields. Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva are also used.

name: Toro
summary: On the Duero in Zamora, a hot, dry continental climate gives red wines made mainly from Tinta de Toro, the local form of Tempranillo. Garnacha plays a smaller part.
label_note: Barrel aged reds may carry Roble, Crianza, Reserva or Gran Reserva. A red named after its grape needs at least 85% of it.

grapes.name: Verdejo
grapes.local_note: Main white variety with Malvasía Castellana
